title: Generator Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the alternator. This part charges the battery and powers the electrical system while the engine runs.
symptoms: Dim lights or a battery that keeps going dead

causes.name: Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the alternator wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the alternator with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a new alternator or a repair to the alternator wiring or connector.

title: Generator Lamp/L-Terminal Circuit
plain: The computer sees a problem in the alternator "L" circuit, which the alternator uses to turn on the charging warning light and signal that it is working.
symptoms: Dim lights or a battery that keeps going dead

causes.name: Damaged wire or corroded connector at the alternator

checks: Check charging voltage with the engine running
Inspect the alternator connector and wiring
fix: Usually a new alternator or a repair to the alternator wiring or connector.

title: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the alternator field circuit. This part lets the computer control how hard the alternator charges.
symptoms: Dim lights or a battery that keeps going dead

causes.name: Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the alternator field circuit wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the alternator field circuit with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a new alternator or a repair to the alternator wiring or connector.

title: Generator Lamp Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem in the circuit it uses to turn the charging system warning light on and off.
symptoms: Battery warning light stays on or never comes on

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem to the instrument cluster

checks: Check that the battery light comes on with the key on and engine off
Test charging voltage to rule out a real charging problem
fix: Usually a wiring repair or instrument cluster repair.

title: Fuel Cap Lamp Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem in the circuit for the "check fuel cap" warning light on the dash.
symptoms: Fuel cap warning light not working or stuck on

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem to the instrument cluster

checks: Check whether the fuel cap light comes on during the startup bulb check
Inspect wiring between the computer and the cluster
fix: Usually a wiring or instrument cluster repair.

title: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the alternator field circuit, often from a wire shorted to ground. This part lets the computer control how hard the alternator charges.
symptoms: Dim lights or a battery that keeps going dead
checks: Inspect the alternator field circuit wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the alternator field circuit with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a new alternator or a repair to the alternator wiring or connector.

title: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit High
plain: The computer sees higher voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the alternator field circuit, often from a wire shorted to power or a failed part. This part lets the computer control how hard the alternator charges.
symptoms: Dim lights or a battery that keeps going dead

causes.name: Faulty or shorted alternator field circuit

checks: Inspect the alternator field circuit wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the alternator field circuit with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a new alternator or a repair to the alternator wiring or connector.

title: Fuel Pump "A" Control Circuit/Open
plain: The computer found a break or problem in the circuit it uses to run the fuel pump, so the engine may not get enough fuel.
symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start

causes.name: Faulty fuel pump driver or control module
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the fuel pump or its module
Blown fuse or failed fuel pump relay

checks: Check the fuel pump fuse and relay
Inspect the connectors at the fuel pump and fuel pump module for corrosion
Check fuel pressure while cranking and running
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair or a new fuel pump control module; sometimes the fuel pump itself.

title: Fuel Pump "A" Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the fuel pump control circuit, often from a wire shorted to ground. This part runs the fuel pump that feeds fuel to the engine.
symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start
checks: Inspect the fuel pump control circuit wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the fuel pump control circuit with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new fuel pump control module or fuel pump.

title: Fuel Pump "A" Control Circuit High
plain: The computer sees higher voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the fuel pump control circuit, often from a wire shorted to power or a failed part. This part runs the fuel pump that feeds fuel to the engine.
symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start

causes.name: Faulty or shorted fuel pump control circuit

checks: Inspect the fuel pump control circuit wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the fuel pump control circuit with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new fuel pump control module or fuel pump.

title: Fuel Pump "A" Control Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The circuit that controls the fuel pump control circuit is not behaving the way the computer expects. This part runs the fuel pump that feeds fuel to the engine.
symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start

causes.name: Corroded connector or high resistance in the wiring

checks: Inspect the fuel pump control circuit wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the fuel pump control circuit with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new fuel pump control module or fuel pump.

title: Internal Control Module Fuel Injector Control Performance
plain: The part of the engine computer that fires the fuel injectors failed a self-check.

causes.name: Shorted fuel injector or injector wiring overloading the driver
Low voltage or poor power and ground connections
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement (a new one usually must be programmed to the car).

title: Internal Control Module Vehicle Speed Performance
plain: The engine computer's internal check of the vehicle speed signal failed.
symptoms: Speedometer or cruise control may act up

causes.name: Erratic vehicle or wheel speed sensor signal
Low voltage or poor power and ground connections
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement (a new one usually must be programmed to the car).

title: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 1
plain: The computer circuit that fires the fuel injectors on bank 1 is not performing correctly.
checks: Check for misfire or injector circuit codes on the same bank
Measure injector resistance and inspect the injector harness
fix: Usually a new injector or wiring repair; sometimes the engine computer.

title: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 2
plain: The computer circuit that fires the fuel injectors on bank 2 is not performing correctly.
checks: Check for misfire or injector circuit codes on the same bank
Measure injector resistance and inspect the injector harness
fix: Usually a new injector or wiring repair; sometimes the engine computer.

title: Internal Control Module EEPROM Error
plain: The engine computer found an error in the memory chip that stores its settings and learned values.
symptoms: Possible reduced power, stalling or no start
Other warning lights may come on

causes.name: Low battery voltage or poor power or ground connections at the computer
Computer software that needs an update or reprogramming
Water damage or corrosion at the computer connector

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement (a new one usually must be programmed to the car).

title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible - ECM/PCM
plain: The engine computer doesn't have this car's vehicle identification number (VIN) stored, or it has the wrong one.
symptoms: Engine may not start on some vehicles

causes.name: Engine computer replaced or reprogrammed without the vehicle ID being set
Used computer from another vehicle installed

checks: Read the stored VIN with a scan tool and compare it with the car
Program the VIN with a dealer-level scan tool
fix: Program the correct VIN into the engine computer.

title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible - TCM
plain: The transmission computer doesn't have this car's vehicle identification number (VIN) stored, or it has the wrong one.
symptoms: Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Transmission computer replaced or reprogrammed without the vehicle ID being set
Used computer from another vehicle installed

checks: Read the stored VIN with a scan tool and compare it with the car
Program the VIN with a dealer-level scan tool
fix: Program the correct VIN into the transmission computer.

title: Odometer Not Programmed - ECM/PCM
plain: The engine computer does not have the vehicle mileage stored, usually after the computer was replaced.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Engine computer replaced or reprogrammed without the vehicle ID being set
Used computer from another vehicle installed

checks: Ask whether the engine computer was recently replaced
Program mileage with a dealer-level scan tool
fix: Program the mileage into the engine computer.

title: Immobilizer Key Not Programmed - ECM/PCM
plain: The engine computer hasn't been paired with the car's anti-theft system and keys, so it may block the engine from starting.
symptoms: Engine will not start, or starts and dies

causes.name: Engine computer replaced without immobilizer pairing
Keys not programmed after computer or module replacement

checks: Ask whether the computer or immobilizer was recently replaced
Have the computer and keys paired with a dealer-level scan tool
fix: Pair the engine computer and keys to the immobilizer system.

title: PCM/ECM/TCM Internal Temperature Too High
plain: A control computer is reporting that it is running too hot inside.
symptoms: Reduced power, limp mode or stalling

causes.name: Shorted sensor, solenoid or actuator overloading the computer
Computer mounted near a heat source or blocked cooling
Low or overheated transmission fluid (computers mounted in the transmission)

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins
fix: Fix any shorted part or heat problem first; otherwise replace and program the computer.

title: Power Steering Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the power steering control circuit. This part controls the steering assist motor or valve on electric or variable-assist power steering.

causes.name: Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the power steering control circuit wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the power steering control circuit with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new power steering control circuit if it tests bad.

title: Power Steering Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the power steering control circuit, often from a wire shorted to ground. This part controls the steering assist motor or valve on electric or variable-assist power steering.
checks: Inspect the power steering control circuit wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the power steering control circuit with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new power steering control circuit if it tests bad.

title: Power Steering Control Circuit High
plain: The computer sees higher voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the power steering control circuit, often from a wire shorted to power or a failed part. This part controls the steering assist motor or valve on electric or variable-assist power steering.

causes.name: Faulty or shorted power steering control circuit

checks: Inspect the power steering control circuit wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the power steering control circuit with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new power steering control circuit if it tests bad.

title: Throttle Actuator Control Range/Performance Bank 1
plain: The electronic throttle on bank 1 isn't opening or closing to the position the computer commands.
symptoms: Reduced power or limp mode warning
Rough, high or low idle, or stalling

causes.name: Faulty electronic throttle body motor or position sensor
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the throttle body

checks: Inspect and clean the throttle body
Check the throttle body connector and wiring
Compare commanded and actual throttle position on a scan tool
Perform a throttle relearn after cleaning
fix: Usually a throttle body cleaning and relearn, or a new electronic throttle body.

title: Throttle Actuator Control Range/Performance Bank 2
plain: The electronic throttle on bank 2 isn't opening or closing to the position the computer commands.
symptoms: Reduced power or limp mode warning

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem at the throttle body

checks: Inspect and clean the throttle body
Compare commanded and actual throttle position on a scan tool
fix: Usually a throttle body cleaning and relearn, or a new electronic throttle body.

title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit
plain: The wire the computer uses to sense the alternator output voltage has a problem, so it may not control charging correctly.

causes.name: Damaged sense wire or corroded connector

checks: Measure charging voltage at the battery with the engine running
Inspect the alternator connector and sense wiring
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new alternator.

title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The wire the computer uses to sense the alternator output voltage is giving a reading that does not make sense, so it may not control charging correctly.

causes.name: Damaged sense wire or corroded connector

checks: Measure charging voltage at the battery with the engine running
Inspect the alternator connector and sense wiring
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new alternator.

title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit Low
plain: The wire the computer uses to sense the alternator output voltage is reading too low, so it may not control charging correctly.
checks: Measure charging voltage at the battery with the engine running
Inspect the alternator connector and sense wiring
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new alternator.

title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit High
plain: The wire the computer uses to sense the alternator output voltage is reading too high, so it may not control charging correctly.
checks: Measure charging voltage at the battery with the engine running
Inspect the alternator connector and sense wiring
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new alternator.

title: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present
plain: While setting itself up, the computer couldn't detect the throttle or gas pedal input it expected.
symptoms: Engine may not start or may stay at idle

causes.name: Unplugged or damaged throttle or pedal sensor connector
Wiring problem in the throttle or pedal circuit
Computer not configured for this vehicle

checks: Check that throttle and pedal connectors are plugged in and undamaged
Confirm the computer is configured for the vehicle
fix: Usually reconnecting or repairing the throttle or pedal wiring, then configuring the computer.

title: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present
plain: While setting itself up, the computer couldn't detect the engine coolant temperature sensor input.

causes.name: Unplugged or damaged coolant temperature sensor connector
Wiring problem in the sensor circuit
Computer not configured for this vehicle

checks: Check that the coolant temperature sensor is plugged in and undamaged
Check the sensor reading on a scan tool
fix: Usually reconnecting or repairing the sensor wiring, or a new coolant temperature sensor.
